scope: Design review of 014-look-inside-a-vocabulary before implementation: spec.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md, decisions.md, against memory/constitution.md and CONTEXT.md, plus targeted reads of controlled_vocabularies/ui/{views,urls,checks}.py, controlled_vocabularies/ui/templates/controlled_vocabularies/ui/conceptscheme_list_item.html, controlled_vocabularies/models.py (ConceptScheme, Concept, ConceptLabel, Collection, static_uri validation), controlled_vocabularies/conf.py, controlled_vocabularies/checks.py, controlled_vocabularies/exchange/skos.py (importer write paths), demo/settings.py, demo/urls.py, tests/test_ui/{test_views.py,test_checks.py}, pyproject.toml [tool.forge.conformance], and the installed mvp package (views/list.py, views/base.py, views/detail.py, templates/list_view.html) to verify plan claims against real upstream behaviour. No code exists for this feature; nothing was built or edited.

findings.claim: [architecture / testing standard §4 test structure] The plan puts VocabularyDetailView's tests in a new file, tests/test_ui/test_detail_view.py, alongside the existing tests/test_ui/test_views.py for the same source module (controlled_vocabularies/ui/views.py) — the exact non-compliant split constitution.md testing standard §4 names by its own worked example.
findings.evidence: memory/constitution.md testing standard §4: 'When one source module defines several units (e.g. multiple models in a single models.py), it stays one tests/test_models.py — the per-unit split is expressed with classes (below), not with extra files (test_concept.py + test_scheme.py alongside a single models.py is non-compliant).' controlled_vocabularies/ui/views.py today defines one unit, VocabularyListView, tested by the one existing tests/test_ui/test_views.py. plan.md 'Files this feature touches' lists controlled_vocabularies/ui/views.py under Changed (VocabularyDetailView added to the same module) but lists tests/test_ui/test_detail_view.py under New, and plan.md's own Constitution Check table claims 'XIV — Test structure | tests/test_ui/ mirrors the source tree; class grouping per behaviour | Complies.' tasks.md T001, T002, T003, T008, T009, T010, T011, T013, T014, T015 and T019 all target tests/test_ui/test_detail_view.py for VocabularyDetailView behaviour — the majority of the feature's tasks. pyproject.toml's [tool.forge.conformance] non-mirror-paths list has no entry for test_detail_view.py, and per constitution.md's own text a path whose subject is a Python module (views.py is) cannot be declared exempt anyway.
findings.suggested_fix: In plan.md and tasks.md, replace every reference to tests/test_ui/test_detail_view.py with tests/test_ui/test_views.py, and organise VocabularyDetailView's tests into new classes inside that one file (e.g. TestVocabularyDetailView, TestVocabularyDetailViewSearch, TestVocabularyDetailViewCollections) rather than a second file. No task's scope changes, only which file its tests land in.

findings.claim: [architecture / naming collision] The plan's queryset annotation name display_label (Key design decision 3, task T009) is identical to Concept's own existing public method Concept.display_label(), and Django sets an annotation as a plain instance attribute, so on every Concept fetched through VocabularyDetailView's queryset the annotation shadows the bound method — a later .display_label() call on one of those instances raises TypeError instead of returning a label.
findings.evidence: controlled_vocabularies/models.py:750 defines def display_label(self) -> str: ... as Concept's documented public accessor. It is called as concept.display_label() from controlled_vocabularies/forms.py:185, controlled_vocabularies/fields.py:294 and :617, and controlled_vocabularies/views.py:168 (the package's own concept-search endpoint) — display_label() is this model's established public convention, not an incidental name. plan.md Key design decision 3 and tasks.md T009/T010 both name the queryset annotation display_label and order by Lower("display_label"). Rendering the page template's {{ object.display_label }} still works (Django's variable resolution finds the shadowed string attribute and, being non-callable, renders it directly) — the defect is latent, not visible in this feature's own template, but reachable the moment any code (plausibly #142's concept page, which this same spec names as the next slice of R6 and will need this exact model) calls .display_label() on an instance obtained via this view's queryset.
findings.reproduction: Given `qs = Concept.objects.filter(scheme=scheme).annotate(display_label=Coalesce(...))` as planned, `concept = qs.first(); concept.display_label()` raises `TypeError: 'str' object is not callable`, whereas `Concept.objects.get(pk=concept.pk).display_label()` (a plain, unannotated fetch) returns the label correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the annotation in plan.md Key design decision 3 and tasks.md T009/T010 to a name that does not collide with the model's own method, e.g. resolved_label — Lower("display_label") becomes Lower("resolved_label") throughout.
